text:
incident-bot: PAGE → P1: gpu-pool `g1` queue length spike + autoscaler at max nodes. queue_length=12540, avg_latency=3.1s, autoscaler_nodes=12/12 (max), prefix_cache_hit=18%. Triggered 1902468000. Dashboard: https://graf.redwood/grafana/d/serve/g1-queue

oncall-tj: picking up. seeing large tail on /generate and /chat. any rolling deploys?

maya: no deploys in last 30m. I can grab the perf dashboard. prefix cache misses spiked at the same time the continuous-batching commit landed ~1902467920. hit rate fell from ~86% -> 18%

carla: that commit changed continuous_batching.max_batch_duration_ms -> 80 (was 40) and bumped max_batch_tokens -> 4096. suspected regression in batching causing oversized batches and KV cache thrash.

kevin: confirmed autoscaler reported OOMs/mismatched evictions on recent pods in g1 pool. kube events: PodEvicted, preemption-like behaviour. Logs: `inference_runner: KV cache miss spike, mem_pressure=true`

oncall-tj: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle high-volume non-enterprise customers 2) rollback continuous-batching change or disable it 3) scale pool beyond max if possible (temp) 4) route critical customers to fallback model variant (cpu/quantized)

luis (cs): visible customer impact: Ledgerly reports 30-120s timeouts on embed + generate since ~11m ago. Several support tickets opened.

carla: i can push a rollback of the batching commit to canary, but for live mitigation we should toggle config first.

oncall-tj: executing quick config patch to reduce burstiness. patching pool config:
```
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 2048    # lowered from 4096
  max_batch_duration_ms: 40 # rollback to previous latency-optimized value
prefix_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 120          # increase TTL to reduce re-population churn
```
Applying via `rwdctl config apply --pool g1 --patch`

oncall-tj: running `rwdctl config apply` now...

incident-bot: CONFIG_APPLY_OK pool=g1 user=oncall-tj ts=1902468042

maya: watching metrics: prefix_cache_hit -> 54% within 60s, queue_length dropping (currently 9.1k), avg_latency 1.8s. good sign but still high.

kevin: autoscaler still at max cap (12). I can request temporary capacity bump with infra: `rwdctl pools scale g1 --max-nodes 18`. need approval from ops-lead.

helena (ops-lead): approve temp bump to 18 nodes. doing request to cloud quota now.

oncall-tj: increasing rate limit for critical customers only, and setting soft throttle for public tenants.
```
rwdctl rate-limit update --customer Ledgerly --rps 15
rwdctl rate-limit update --tenant public --rps 50 --soft
```

luis (cs): Ledgerly CS notified and applied a temporary reduced concurrency on their side; they confirm improved success rate for embeddings but still occasional 5-10s latencies.

incident-bot: CLOUD_QUOTA_INC_REQUESTED ticket=INC-4321 ts=1902468070

maya: queue_length now 4.6k, avg_latency 910ms, prefix_cache_hit 71%. autoscaler still provisioning new nodes (if quota approved).

carla: long-term fix: revert the batching heuristics change and add a canary gating for prefix-cache hit regression. Also need a test harness for cache cold-start behaviour when batching params change.

kevin: opened follow-up runbook items: increase evictions logging, add autoscaler alert for "at-max-with-growing-queue" and force a circuit to fallback model variants when prefix_cache_hit < 30%.

oncall-tj: handoff to helena in 1902468120 — I'll stay until quota/warm nodes in place.

helena (ops-lead): taking over. current state summary: queue_length=3.2k, avg_latency=670ms, prefix_cache_hit=78%, customers impacted reduced to intermittent issues for Ledgerly. cloud quota request pending.

pagerduty: INCIDENT STATUS → acked by helena at 1902468122.

carla: assigning postmortem owner: carla. action items:
- rollback batching heuristics PR and add canary gating (owner: carla)
- add autoscaler "stuck at max" alert (owner: kevin)
- implement prefix-cache integration test & regression alert (owner: maya)
- run customer impact sweep, ensure CS outreach to Ledgerly (owner: luis)

luis (cs): i'll follow up with Ledgerly and share ETA on mitigation + runbook for customers to reduce concurrency while we stabilize.

helena (ops-lead): leaving follow-up on-call to night shift. next_update_due 1902468600.

oncall-tj: final notes: root cause seems to be an overly-aggressive batching change that increased batch sizes and churned the prefix cache, combined with autoscaler hitting configured max capacity. cascade: larger batches -> KV cache misses -> memory pressure -> pod evictions -> autoscaler tries to add nodes but hit account quota -> queue grows -> throttles & customer timeouts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigations in place; monitoring) resolved_by=oncall-tj helena carla ts=1902468198

helena (ops-lead): postmortem kickoff scheduled in #postmortems tomorrow 10:00PT. logs/snapshots saved under s3://redwood-incidents/1902468000/"
